✔ Understand situations
✔ Think logically
✔ Solve problems
✔ Make decisions
✔ Adapt to new environments.

INTELLIGENCE
“Artificial Intelligence (AI) 
is the branch of computer 
science that enables 
machines to perform 
tasks that normally 
require human 
intelligence, such as 
learning, reasoning, 
problem solving, decision 
making, perception, and 
language understanding”.

ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE - VIEWS
Think like human Think Rationally
Act like human Act Rationally
Like human - Tries to imitate humans, May make human-like mistakes
Rationally - Makes decisions based on logic and goals, Tries to achieve the best outcome

• The definitions of AI gives four possible goals to pursue :
1. Systems that think like humans
2. Systems that think rationally
3. Systems that act like humans
4. Systems that act rationally

AGENTS
• An agent is anything that can be viewed as perceiving its environment through sensors 
and acting upon that environment through actuators.
• Human agent: Eyes, ears, and other organs for sensors
 Hands, legs, mouth, and other body parts for actuators
• Robotic agent: Cameras and infrared range finders for sensors
 Various motors for actuators

RATIONAL AGENTS
• Always tries to choose the best possible action to achieve its goal.
“For each possible percept sequence, a rational agent should select an action that is expected to 
maximize its performance measure, given the evidence provided by the percept sequence and 
whatever built-in knowledge the agent has”.
• Performance Measure : Criterion used to evaluate how successfully an agent achieves its goal.

AGENT TYPES
Four basic types in order of increasing generality:
• Simple reflex agents
• Model-based reflex agents
• Goal-based agents
• Utility-based agents
• Learning Agent

rects.text: Four basic types in order of increasing generality:

slides.text:
SIMPLE REFLEX AGENTS
“A Simple Reflex Agent selects an action 
based only on the current percept (current 
situation) using predefined condition–action 
rules.”
• It does not remember the past and does not 
think about the future.

rects.text: “A Simple Reflex Agent selects an action
based only on the current percept (current

slides.text:
MODEL-BASED REFLEX AGENTS
“Model-Based Reflex Agent maintains an 
internal state (memory) of the environment 
and uses both the current percept and past
information to decide the next action”.
State - stores what the agent already knows.

GOAL-BASED AGENTS
Model-Based Reflex Agent: "What should I do 
now?"
Goal-Based Agent: "Which action will help me reach 
my goal?“
“A Goal-Based Agent selects actions that help it 
achieve a predefined goal by considering the future 
consequences of its actions”.

rects.text: “A Goal-Based Agent selects actions that help it
achieve a predefined goal by considering the future

slides.text:
UTILITY-BASED AGENTS
A Goal-Based Agent asks, "Will I reach the goal?"
A Utility-Based Agent asks, "Which option is the
BEST among all the options?“
“A Utility-Based Agent selects the action that maximizes 
its utility (or happiness/value) among all possible 
actions.”
• Selects the action that maximizes utility
• Evaluates all possible outcomes
• Uses a utility function to assign a value (score) to 
each possible state
• Chooses the action with the highest utility

• Most advanced type of intelligent

"A Learning Agent not only performs

decisions.“
• Learns from experience and 
feedback. Improves its performance 
over time.

ENVIRONMENT TYPES
• Fully Observable Vs Partially Observable
• Deterministic Vs Stochastic
• Episodic Vs Sequential
• Static Vs Dynamic
• Discrete Vs Continuous
• Single Agent Vs Multiagent

PARTIALLY OBSERVABLE
The agent can observe the complete 
state of the environment at every point in 
time.
FULLY OBSERVABLE
Example: Chess
• All pieces are visible. 
• Nothing is hidden from the agent. 
• Complete information available
The agent has limited information
about the environment; some parts are 
hidden or unknown.
Example: Self-driving Car
• Objects behind buildings, vehicles, or 
corners are not visible to the agent. 
• Incomplete information available

slides.text:
Stochastic
The same action always produces the 
same result.
Deterministic
Example: Vacuum Cleaner Robot
• The robot moves right. 
• It always reaches the right room. 
• The outcome is predictable. 
• Predictable outcome
The same action may produce 
different results due to uncertainty.
Example: Self-driving Car / Taxi Driver
o The car turns left. 
o A pedestrian may appear. 
o Traffic may increase. 
o Another vehicle may suddenly enter. 
o Uncertain outcome

rects.text: It always reaches the right room.

slides.text:
Sequential
Each decision is independent of previous 
decisions.
Episodic
Example: Defective Part Inspection
• The camera inspects one product. 
• It decides Good or Defective. 
• The next product is inspected 
independently. 
• Independent decisions
Each decision affects future decisions.
Example: Chess
• Every move changes the board. 
• The next move depends on the previous 
move. 
• Wrong decisions affect future outcomes.

rects.text: The next move depends on the previous

slides.text:
Dynamic
The environment does not change while 
the agent is making a decision.
Static
Example: Crossword Puzzle
• The puzzle remains the same while you 
think. 
• Nothing changes automatically. 
• You have enough time to decide.
Environment remains unchanged
The environment can change while the 
agent is making a decision.
Example: Self-driving Car / Taxi Driver
• Traffic keeps moving. 
• Pedestrians may suddenly cross. 
• Traffic lights change. 
• The agent must react continuously. 
Environment changes continuously

Continuous
Finite or countable number of states 
and actions.
Discrete
Example: Chess
• Limited number of pieces. 
• Fixed squares (64). 
• A move is from one square to 
another. 
• Countable states and actions
continuously changing states, actions, or 
time.
Example: Self-driving Car
• Speed can be 25.1, 25.2, 25.25 km/h...
• Steering angle changes continuously. 
• Position changes every second. 
• Time flows continuously. 
• Infinite possible values

Multiagent
Only one intelligent agent is involved in 
making decisions.
Example: Sudoku
• Only one player solves the puzzle. 
• No opponent exists. 
• The environment does not compete 
with the agent. 
 Only one decision-maker
Two or more intelligent agents interact, 
cooperate, or compete with each other.
Example: Chess
• Two players make decisions. 
• One player's move affects the other.
• Both agents try to achieve their own 
goal. 
 Multiple decision-makers

patterns from data and improve their performance without being explicitly programmed.”

• Identifies hidden patterns. 
• Makes predictions or decisions. 
• Improves performance over time. 
Real-Life Examples
 3 Types:
• Supervised
• Unsupervised
• Reinforcement

Data Science
Data Science is an interdisciplinary field that combines statistics, machine learning, 
programming, and domain knowledge to extract meaningful insights from data and 
support better decision-making.
• Collects data from various sources
• Cleans and preprocesses data
• Analyzes data to discover patterns
• Builds predictive models using Machine

decision-making
